tier_reason: C stands; still flagged not faster than C Brotli.

corrections.tradeoffs: Memory-safe (library description says all included code is safe), no_std capable with a pluggable allocator, SECCOMP-friendly front-loaded allocation, multithreaded compression, catable streams, C-compatible FFI, custom dictionaries. Encoder is stated to be bitwise identical to the C compressor at quality 0-9. BrotliEncoderParams::default() sets quality 11 (issue #93 open); in the one-shot compressor quality 10 stands for the '9.5' mode, not C's quality 10. The unsafe feature (no bounds checks) lives only in the brotli-decompressor crate; brotli 9.0 has none of its own. Cost is decoder speed: the decompressor README lists an extra indirection in the hgroups, array bounds checks on every access and no aligned 64/128-bit loads from [u8] as expected losses.
corrections.caveats: Enricher: brotli 9.0.0 pins brotli-decompressor ~6.0, so it cannot pick up the 6.1.0 and 6.1.1 decoder releases (crates.io, 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-21); every measurement predates them. The android-doctor 4.65 s versus 2.28 s figure is end-to-end against vendored libbrotli 1.1.0, not pure decode, and that project then switched to the C library. The brotli-decompressor 6.0.0 changelog says its code was AI-authored.
